qc1.pitchdeck.io · editor · 17 Aug 2026

Editor icons still on the old pack

Mani flagged that the editor runs two icon packs and that its icons still look thin. It is actually three delivery methods. Here is every icon in the editor that is not Phosphor, where it lives, and what it should become.

41non-Phosphor icons found in the editor
31have a direct Phosphor match
6worth a look before swapping
4have no Phosphor equivalent

What is actually going on

1

A second icon pack called appicon. A custom icon font (appicon.woff) with 699 glyphs, thin and hand drawn, nothing to do with Phosphor. In the editor it owns the slide right-click menu, the text toolbar, the text properties panel and the image toolbar. This is the thin look. Several of its class names no longer describe what they draw, for example ic_trim_video renders Cut and ic_save_slide_as_template renders Paste.

2

The Phosphor icons are the old delivery, at two different weights. Every SVG icon in the editor is legacy phosphor-react markup (a 256 background rect plus stroked paths), not the Phosphor font we ship in design-system/icons. Weights are mixed on the same screen: 11 icons render at bold and 35 at regular. Sizes are mixed too, 12, 16, 18 and 20 px, against a steady 20 px on the dashboard.

3

Slide status uses loose SVG files. The five status icons are <img> tags pointing at /docs/assets/images/status/. Their colour is baked into the file, so it cannot follow a token and it cannot respond to theme.

The clearest proof, one command, two packs

Duplicate slide appears in both the right-click menu and the bottom bar overflow menu. Same command, same product, two different icon sets. This is the two packs Mani is describing, side by side.

The clipboard block, resolved

Cut, Copy, Paste and Duplicate sit within two rows of each other, and the obvious Phosphor picks made three of the four the same rounded rectangle. At 18 px in a vertical menu, silhouette is what you scan, not metaphor. So the four were chosen to have four different outlines.

before

Copy and Duplicate identical, Paste a third rectangle
after

blades, two squares, ruled board, stacked cards

Copy keeps the universal two-squares icon, which is the shape people already know. The differentiation comes from the other two: Paste gains ruled lines, and Duplicate moves off the clipboard metaphor onto a stack of cards, which is what it actually does. Full comparison is in clipboard-icon-options.html next to this page.

Slide status, a third delivery

The five status icons in this menu are not font glyphs at all. They are standalone files under /docs/assets/images/status/, loaded as <img> tags, which means their colour is baked into the file and cannot follow a token. Phosphor covers all five, and moving them to the font puts the colour back under CSS.

The one thing still open

Phosphor has no uppercase, title case or lowercase icon. The text case row in Text properties uses four old glyphs and only one of them has a home in Phosphor.

none
uppercase
titlecase
lowercase

Recommendation: stop treating these as icons. Render the row as four text buttons, which is what Figma and Google Docs do, and it reads faster than any glyph can:

NoneAAAaaa

That also frees ph-text-aa for the font size control in the text toolbar, which is the only other place it fits. The alternative is keeping four appicon glyphs alive purely for this row, which means the old font never gets deleted.

Weight audit

finding 2

Distinct Phosphor icons in the editor by the stroke width baked into their markup. Regular is 16. Anything at 24 is rendering bold next to icons that are not.

Stroke width in markupReads asIcons
16Regular, correct35
24Bold, too heavy11
filledFill weight3

Audited on qc1.pitchdeck.io, deck 390121, on 17 Aug 2026. Old glyphs above are rendered from the live appicon.woff; replacements are rendered from design-system/icons/Phosphor.woff2, so what you see is what you get.

Slide thumbnail hover icons were confirmed in the DOM but not captured on screen, so check those two in context.
